What an amazing start from Lendl; awesome in the literal sense as well.
Lendl is really aggressive today; stepping in and taking the ball early. He usually likes to hover around or just behind the baseline; but today he's really taking the ball early.
Looks like Lendl has left the 'everything goes in' mode; but he's up a break already; so coasting on serve is enough.
The reverse angle shows the return catching the line; and Lendl; just full of confidence at this stage; goes for a clean winner and makes it!
Finally a great point by Edberg.

Edberg moving halfway forward from the baseline after hitting a great angled backhand; and then volleying from the service line and moving to net; results in a volley approach shot. Quite a rarity; and takes superb skills to pull off and win the point.

Edberg thought his 1st serve was an ace - even the commentators thought so - but would rather not argue with the umpire. Still; it clearly bothered him; and two quick errors followed to bring up deuce.
In the last six years; Edberg has won more matches - 424; to be precise - than any other player.
Edberg's anticipation working wonders.
Lendl's smash goes straight at Edberg; who fends it off impressively with sheer reflexes; but still loses the point.
Edberg changes his racquet after double-faulting.
[Stefan Edberg first four rounds: 92 winners at net.]
[Ivan Lendl first four rounds: 31 aces.]
And Lendl should go to his bag and change racquets; as he usually does at the ball change; and in fact; he's going to do that. The routine he rigidly sticks to.
Excellent defence at net by Edberg. Had to volley low on return and the next shot; yet put the ball deep; then volleyed it away on a change of direction.
Lendl responds like a champ; respect.
For some reason the Lendl fans are more numerous/active this time. There's a lot of I-van! I-van! between the games; and not a lot of the usual Ste-fan Ed-berg! chant.
[Stefan Edberg first four rounds: 76 backhand errors.]
Lendl's 84% 1st serve win has been the key stat so far; but now the match is about to turn upside down.
This might be the key moment when he's serving for a two sets to love lead. We'll see.
Apparently someone in the stands took a flash photo during the point; which distracted Lendl.
A plane flies low over the court just as Edberg is about to serve; forcing him to abort his service motion and start anew.
[Stefan Edberg first four rounds: 6 double faults.]
Really wasn't an approach shot; but when he saw he had his opponent stretching; moved in anyway.
Edberg moonballing Lendl on the forehand side again and winning the point; amazing.

Lendl is showed picking up the racquet he's thrown away in a momentary fit of rage. Nobody expected such a turnaround; least of all Lendl himself. Edberg will ride the wave of confidence now for another set.
Angry Lendl hitting the ball out HARD; eliciting some boos from the crowd. Lendl [is] lucky; I think; not be given a ball abuse warning there.
Edberg lets out a rare cry of frustration; having missed triple BP twice in a row.
Lendl threw a sudden deep floaty backhand for a change of pace/spin; and Edberg didn't adjust well enough.

Lendl mistook the squeal of Edberg's shoes (rubbing against the hard surface when he adjusted his return position) for the double fault alarm and stopped playing; although it would've been tough for him to reach the angled return anyway. The umpire confirmed the alarm did not go off; so Lendl had to accept it was his own fault.
Poor move by Lendl; volleying deep shots is not his game.
The ball might have well been in; but there was no disputing close calls; of course.
Lendl's netcord jumps high and lands right on the baseline; but the lineswoman erroneously calls 'out'. The umpire corrects the call immediately and orders the point to be replayed; as per protocol.
Lendl checking the service line and giving a long hard look to the area where the serve landed; wondering if it was actually a double fault. Looked like it just touched the line.
Nice wrongfooting.
A fairly poor approach; but incredible movement at net wins Edberg the second successive point. The crowd applauds heartily.
Funny: rival fan groups competing whose chant is louder; I-van! or Ste-fan!.
Edberg trying to surprise Lendl with the drop shot approach; but it's a bit too deep; and Lendl responds with a slice that lands on the sideline. Excellent stuff.
Great backhand winner from outside the court. The crowd is roaring.
Quite fittingly; Edberg's run of 18 consecutive service points won ends on a double fault.
Lendl gets his first lob winner; I think. He doesn't let Edberg's hold streak get into his head.

Edberg throwing moonball forehands again until Lendl mistimes the high slice. It's still funny; considering Edberg's image as a very attacking player; which he was; but that doesn't mean he couldn't push on defence.
Suddenly Lendl produces a great slice return like he hasn't done since the previous set.
Some great kick 2nd serves from Edberg recently; like this one.
A tough low chip return from Lendl; but Edberg executes a supreme half-volley.

The lineswoman mistakenly calls 'out' too early; then corrects herself right away; but the point still has to be replayed; of course. Lendl tells her to 'let it bounce first'. As the commentator explained; the serve was actually starting out wide; but with a lot of spin it curved inside the line.
...Edberg is probably still on the way up or approaching his peak; and Lendl probably just passed his. There has never been a time when clueless comments were not a thing; has there?
Huge mishit by Lendl. The volley was high; allowing great time to adjust and swing freely - and he just botched it. Looks like Lendl's game is about to go south.
Superb backhand flick from Lendl; just a bit too high/late to be called a true half-volley; but still very impressive.

Lendl is done physically; the Australian heat has drained him. He is nearing the end of his prime and doesn't have the same endurance as even the year before; when he was able to outlast Edberg in the fifth set. A point like this one; trying to volley in no-man's land; shows that Lendl has effectively given up. Nothing wrong with it - coming back from this position is impossible when your opponent is clearly fresher. All that's left is get the game of honour; avoiding a shameful bagel; and be done with it.
Ivan Lendl has really played some fine tennis in this match; but in patches - terrific for a set and a half; strong fourth set...

Those were some massive kick serves; Lendl couldn't return them with interest.
Lendl stalling quite a bit before serving (in modern tennis; that would be just the normal preparation time...). And then a double fault - how appropriate.
Once again; Lendl taking time; rubbing his eyes repeatedly before serving. This time it pays off; and he seals the tiebreak.
A superb backhand right into the corner.
Edberg kicks a patch of grass in a rare showing of frustration. He's only 19 here; after all.
A failed drop shot volley attempt.
Lendl cries something about these bounces being 'disgusting'. He's missed a lot of makeable 2nd serve returns so far; but was great when it mattered during the tiebreak.
Lendl with another angry yell. Even spits on the grass; causing a few boos from the stands.

No applause from the crowd; but I think Edberg should be credited with a forced error here; because the serve was quite angled; forcing Lendl to reach further to the right and into an uncomfortable return position.
Edberg a bit unsteady on his feet as well at times; the court is really tough to play on; I can see why they changed the venue & surface.
Lendl wrongfooting Edberg nicely; the latter having expected a crosscourt shot.
Edberg showcasing his agility again; but Lendl's clutch half-volley comes right at his feet.
Philippe Chatrier is also watching the match; or at least he's there in the stands.
A meek lob from Lendl; should have gone for the kill; but the unexpected depth Edberg got on that tough half-volley evidently made Lendl uncertain.

Gee; that was a frighteningly primal scream from the Czech. The commentators think he probably said 'NO LUCK!'. That makes sense; as Lendl's 2nd serve returns hitting the top of the net happened several times already; plus Edberg got that lucky net cord on the previous point. That serve kicked high; though; so it's a forced error.
Lendl throws his racquet on the ground; but picks it up quickly (no hissy fits there). Nothing good for the racquet; is it?
What a massive kicker! Lendl isn't too happy with the call; but no further argument follows.
Edberg kicks the ball high into the air.
Actually that was a great curved return while being pushed way wide; only a bit too long. Would've been miraculous for that to go in.
There's the racquet head speed! Cannonball FH winner.
Edberg using his sliding skills again - the slice just barely failed to clear the net.
Lendl is positioned in the no-man's land; expecting a short reply; but Edberg's forehand on the run is good and deep; which shocks Lendl; who falls down trying to reach it.
Lendl channels his displeasure into two very deep and powerful backhands that Edberg cannot handle.
A terrific low volley by Edberg lands near the baseline; causing a weak lob from Lendl that Edberg easily smashes.
Right now both are standing at the same number of points won for the match as well as the second set specifically. Edberg is about to make the crucial break and then routine Lendl in the 3rd set.
0-40. Correction; 15-30. Lendl nods approvingly.
Edberg jerked to his right to meet the ball; but slipped and nearly fell; resulting in a 'cheap' ace.
Edberg is quite annoyed with himself; flailing his racquet and muttering something under his breath.

Lendl takes some extra 20 seconds before serving; repeatedly rubbing his eyes; wiping his forehead; even adjusting the pockets of his shorts - and then he loses grip of the ball when bouncing it; adding another 5 seconds to the preparation. Clearly Lendl is tense; and it shows: first when he hits a cautious backhand at net instead of volleying; and then when Edberg smartly fires right at his body; Lendl moves awkwardly and can't get it right; suddenly losing the touch he showed previously (despite never being the most natural volleyer).
Lendl would rather stay back at this crucial time; as that's his best game. /// Edberg slides and trips on the slippery court.
A sarcastic jab from the stands; to which Lendl replies simply; Shut up.
Lendl slams his racquet against the ground after a way long 2nd serve gives Edberg the first break of the match. Many more to follow as Lendl will struggle to find his aim.
The crowd was initially neutral; but (likely thanks to Lendl's angry antics) is now firmly on Edberg's side; cheering loudly whenever he wins a point.
A great angled ace in the wind. Edberg doesn't even cross the service line; because it's immediately obvious Lendl isn't getting anywhere close to the ball.
The cheeky drop volley is a bit too much - netted.
Right on the line; making the chalk fly up.
Three aces in one game! Edberg is on fire now.
0-15; ball was long. Lendl is just pissed.
Lendl intentionally trying to lob Edberg on the return; now that's a very rare tactic.
A great kicker right on the T. Inspired serving from Edberg under pressure so far; minus the tiebreak.
Another very deep volley from Edberg; the genius is already showing.
The ball dropped in the very corner; risky stuff.
That was a difficult smash; Edberg had to step back and hit it - well done.
Lendl has been spitting on the grass every so often recently; seems like there's some discomfort.
The net cord messed with Lendl's timing and caused a shallow lob volley; easy prey for Edberg.
A superb low backhand winner.

Between the sets: under the heavily overcast sky; Lendl claims he hurt his knee and asks for an injury timeout. When the umpire doesn't budge; announcing fifteen seconds; Lendl outright demands a timeout and calls for the Grand Prix superviser; who apparently suggests that Lendl be allowed a quick knee massage. Meanwhile Edberg puts on a jacket and jogs around waiting until they are done. When time is called again a few minutes later; Lendl returns to the court with no obvious trouble.
Chalk flies up again; pinpoint accuracy.
Again a great low BH winner; right on the sideline.
Lendl appears to have regained his composure during the time-out; and is back to fighting through the match.
A perfect super deep volley under pressure.
Edberg raises hands apologetically and then puts them on the back of his head; astonished at that slice of luck (the net cord volley dropped dead on the other side).
He let it go; Edberg; had a play on that ball.
Edberg's hair dancing in the heavy wind. It is a great mark on the players that they maintained a generally high level of play despite the difficult conditions.
Edberg drops the racquet on the ground; with an adorably disappointed look on his face that reminds us he is still a teenager.
Quality pass under pressure; parallel to the sideline.
Edberg stays back on the 2nd serve again; but Lendl immediately reminds him this will not work by going to the net himself and winning the point with chip-and-charge tactics.
An impressive running forehand.
Lendl tripped when volleying and fell on the ground head-first.
Lendl; perhaps seeking to ensure good footing; volleys too close to the net and gets lobbed beautifully.
Lendl unhappy about... the call; the court; the weather; the crowd - I guess all of it - complaining harshly to the umpire; but so far play continues.
The crowd reacts to Lendl's feisty attitude by giving prolonged cheering to Edberg's next ace.
That's the sort of situation here for the crowd that they really like.
The crowd outright boos Lendl after he hits the netted ball out. By this point; he has completely antagonised them.
They still applaud his winners; though. That's nice and fair.
Finally the supervisor comes out and motions for the umpire to announce a weather break. Lendl applauds with his racquet sarcastically to the boos of the crowd.
Some time later; the sky clears up enough for the match to be resumed. Lendl comes out ready to rumble; showcasing his ability with a delightful forehand pass on the run.
Lendl stretches wide for the slice that amazingly touches the line.
He's pretty cool; young Stefan Edberg. Funny to the modern ear.
Chalk flies up off the service line; but Lendl still manages to get the return in play; and then hits a nice lob to force the error.
A sensational pick-up there from Lendl. A breath-taking low volley off a powerful return.
Edberg misses the ball toss before the 2nd serve; lets it bounce; then restarts the service routine again.
Great return - just high enough that Edberg did not catch it with his racquet and low enough to land before the baseline.
Lendl fired the backhand pass right at Edberg; who thought it was too high and elected to duck down; but the ball landed on the baseline. Some terrific play from Lendl in this game.

Nice to note that both players are given simple chairs to sit during the changeovers; and it's fine. Lendl drinks a little water from the glass brought by a ballboy; Edberg - some tonic beverage from his bottle.
Irritated Edberg hits the racquet against the ground. Again; a reminder that even the beacon of sportsmanship was a little fiery in his youth - but only a little.
Supreme nimbleness and reflexes from Edberg; producing a magical half-volley that completely reverses the point. The crowd roars in delight when Edberg wins it.
A finely calibrated first volley from Edberg against a heavy low angled return. Right into the corner - Lendl could only respond with a lob; then Edberg wrapped it up.
Lendl hits the service line twice in one point: first with his serve; then with the final smash.
Strong coverage of the net by Edberg.
A brave 2nd serve from Edberg here; bounced near the service line.

Lendl didn't expect that Edberg would manage to volley that return back down the line and hesitated for a split second; ended up being a bit too late to the ball to hit a good pass reliably; tried a lob and missed long.
Lendl's face grows gloomier with each game.
Lendl volleys deep; but Edberg is still able to control the ball and set up a pass.
No angry gestures from Edberg; he just looks annoyed.
Probably Lendl's best net point of the match; great defending.
Another Lendl yell.
Excellent volleying from Edberg and great athleticism from Lendl; lunging desperately to get that smash back; and it wasn't that far from going in.

Edberg's return jams Lendl and forces a weak half-volley that Edberg hits an easy bullet forehand off - Lendl anticipates the direction correctly and amazingly manages to make a decent volley; but the shot was just too huge.

Lendl hits a safe 2nd serve; but still approaches the net; keeping the intimidation factor. Edberg tries to make a direct return winner and misses by about two inches; then falls to the ground in despair (picking himself up quickly; of course).
Again Lendl takes his time to get ready to serve - that's the mental game.
Lendl's brilliant half-volley lands near the baseline; Edberg; retreating; has a second to think and decides to go for a blistering pass rather than a safe lob; but hits the top of the net.
What a bad miss by Edberg; must be nerves. He drops the racquet in astonishment (and picks it up quickly as well; no antics here).
A very low return forces the error; and it's danger time for Edberg.
Edberg's 2nd serves have been top notch in this match (except that one game with 4 DFs).
NO! cries Lendl in vain.

More angry actions from Lendl: he throws the racquet on the ground; then catches it by the frame and hits the ground with it again; and again finishes by spitting. No way a player would be allowed to spit on the court so much now.
Great speed from Edberg; although he still couldn't control the lob.
Lendl lunges for the ball and slips pretty badly. The crowd shouts as he gets up; they want to see him lose.
The crowd roars. Match points for Edberg!
Edberg steps back to prepare his swing - and nets it. Tension is in the air.
That was actually a quality 2nd serve; hit deep and bouncing near the service line; but Edberg found a masterful return.

Edberg's sharp return forces a weak volley from Lendl; Edberg runs up to it; Lendl guesses wrong by covering the crosscourt direction and can only watch Edberg's DTL ball fly... and sail out of court. Peak drama now.
The perfect ace! Completely unreturnable.
Another terrific serve; and Lendl holds after saving three MPs.

Lendl sprints to Edberg's drop volley; bends too far to get to the ball and falls badly on his left knee - that was worse than the previous stumbles. Doesn't injure himself outright; but there's a clear discomfort. He takes time to wipe the chalk off the knee; then slowly goes back to the baseline; bends and stretches his left leg to check whether it's okay. There are shouts from some people in the audience who must think he's wasting time. Lendl; with a smug look on his face; responds by flipping them off with the racquet handle; causing a surprised 'ooh' as well as a few boos; but also some applause - the Aussies like it spicy; ha.

The umpire announces; Ladies and gentlemen. The final of men's singles championship of Australia; match between J. Connors - J. Newcombe. Best of five sets. Connors has won the toss and elected to serve. ... Linesmen ready. Ballboys ready. Players ready. Play.
Connors had no reason to look happy as he fell down trying to chase the angled return. Not a great start for Jimbo at all.
Great serve - skidded off the line and under Newcombe's racquet as he swung through the air.
Interestingly; the umpire announces Advantage server rather than Advantage Connors. I wonder when that changed.
Rod; if you're watching; best of luck to you in the Las Vegas match against Jimmy Connors in February. Very nice of the Aussie commentator team.
What disguise! Fooled Connors completely.
Fun comment here: Unlike previous matches; his [Connors's] shirt is out; and he couldn't care less.
Probably a bad bounce. Connors joking light-heartedly about his great spin - amusing to see the supposed brat in such a jovial mood.
Somebody in the crowd making a smart comment; which Jimmy didn't greatly appreciate. Ha!
Newcombe let the ball go - and it landed right on the baseline.

During the changeover; Connors soaks the handle of his racquet in water and then wipes it clean. The commentators suppose that has to do with the abundance of flies on court; that players have to brush off before serving every so often.
By the way; very nice of the audience to give players mild applause when they leave their chairs to go back on court. Shows their appreciation.

Connors; hoping for the lob to go out; hesitated a bit before running to the baseline; and; as a result; got there too late and missed the smash. His confidence is a bit unsteady; causing an occasional unforced error or a poor decision; which will prove to be crucial in deciding the match.
Connors is so frustrated with the wild miss that he hits himself in the head with his racquet. Could've pressured Newcombe there; instead he's going to get broken now...
A very sweet smash drop shot from Newcombe there.
Although Newcombe lost that exciting exchange; his deep lobs made Connors doubt himself; as seen in the following points.
Connors emits what the commentator aptly describes as the wail of the banshee.
Again Connors guesses wrong. Newcombe really has a fearsome serve when it's on.
Wrongfooting Jimmy even on second serve; masterful.
Newcombe blowing his nose into a handkerchief he kept in his pocket as he walks back to the baseline. Tennis was really cosy back then!

Some more light-hearted banter on court between the two; much to the crowd's amusement. But being too soft probably contributed to Connors's loss in the end. I guess that's why he would later put up the brat act to win.
Cheeky smash drop shot from Connors there.
Amazing volley off even a weak smash!
Commentators during the changeover: Newcombe says he was seven pounds overweight when he started the tournament.
Connors smiling and shouting I can't get that one; too! when he sees the smash go past him.
Connors is taking a lot of time; he's slowed down his service preparation.
An audible Ah; dammit! from Connors.
Connors puts on an angry show - I can't get that! is followed by a racquet throw. Picking it up; he makes a belated 'Very good!' acknowledgement; prompting some giggles from the crowd.

The commentating team giving a great deal of praise to Newcombe's SF win over Roche - 11-9 in the fifth after coming back from 2-5; saving 4 MPs. Apparently Newcombe was so immersed in the match he didn't remember he saved match points until they told him.
Lucky shank for Newcombe; but Connors gets a lucky net cord of his own.
Cat and mouse? More like claycourt tennis.
This match is completely 50/50. Indeed it is - not only are the players one break & set apiece; they both stand at 80 points won right now. The next game will prove to be crucial...

A questionable call. Newcombe gives a long hard look to the linesman and then the umpire; but doesn't say anything yet. The commentators think the ball was probably out - looked suspicious to me as well; but there was no disputing calls back then.
Newcombe is skeptical after the previous call; but it's clearly a bit long this time. Connors mockingly spreads his arms wide to show how 'big' the distance between the baseline and the ball was.

The crowd's applause quickly turns into an uproar as Newcombe signals great indignation by putting a palm over his face; then holding it close to his racquet; indicating how long he thought the ball was. There are shots of 'Fault!' and general whistling while Newcombe mumbles annoyedly under his breath; and Connors is just standing there akimbo with a thoughtful look. The umpire; untouched (as is his duty); announces mildly: 'Forty-fifteen... Forty-fifteen!'; which is met by a wave of booing from the stands (with one woman very loudly shouting 'Oh - my - God!'; funny); as Newcombe and Connors walk back to their returning/serving spots; respectively. Great atmosphere for a Slam final; ha.

Even though the last one was probably a good serve (the commentating team agrees); the one at 0-15 probably wasn't; and Jimmy; who is apparently feeling much too jovial today; decides to throw in an intentional double fault to appease the crowd; which responds with excited cheering and lasting applause until Connors gestures for them to stop. Won't keep some from distracting him later; though. I think that was too kind of Connors - he got soft and thus distracted himself (losing some of the crucial mental focus); gave Newcombe mental advantage; and showed that crowd reaction could pressure him into self-defeating decisions. No wonder he got broken afterwards. I fancy that must have been a big lesson for Jimbo going forward. Still a great match; anyway.

Connors continues to flirt with the crowd; making a funny gesture after missing the first serve - only for some boor to suggest 'Double fault!' as he is about to hit the second. Finally the umpire intervenes and tells spectators to be 'quiet; please'; but the damage is done already.
Newcombe making very intelligent use of the wind that hinders Connors's power game.
Although Connors was certainly rattled; the last three points were all great from Newcombe; so he deserved that break.
Both players often bounce the ball just once or twice before serving - great to see.

Sedgman (as part of the commentator trio) is asked to deliver an opinion as a former pro player; and says that it is common to respect the umpire's decision; especially in a big match - throwing points away deliberately is not viewed as an obligation.

The trick shot from Newcombe was a no-look lob with his back to the court - quality stuff! // ...Game Connors. He leads 5 games to 3. Baffled silence makes the umpire realise his mistake. Correction. Newcombe leads 5 games to 3. A round of applause ensues. Connors seems slightly irritated.
The commentators count 9 aces and 5 doubles for Newcombe; 3 aces and 0 doubles for Connors. Apparently neither the controversial ace nor the intentional double fault that followed are included.
The crowd is firmly behind Newcombe now. A disappointing 'Aww!' when he nets that volley.
Newk let himself be softballed. An interesting way of putting it.
The crowd produces a mighty roar of delight.
This match is being played in remarkably fine spirit. Credit to both players.
Both players regularly have to brush flies away from the face; especially Connors. Unthinkable to allow such a hindrance on court now.
Connors yells in frustration after missing the last shot; then shakes his head irritably. Not so jovial now; naturally.
Observation: Newcombe always gets up from his chair a bit earlier than Connors at the end of the changeover.
Awfully struck serve. Love the commentators' blunt honesty. They also called Connors's backhand return 'glorious'; so no lack of praise for him either - all fair.
A deafening roar and lasting applause from the audience; they are totally into it.
Newcombe takes extra time before serving to brush off flies. Probably a bit of stalling; but really flies have been bothering the players throughout the whole match.
Newcombe even jumped in exasperation when he saw the volley land wide; that's how badly he wanted it over.
Newk slipped and fell in vain chase; then took some time to get up and pull himself together before another service point. Wasn't hurt; just grazed.
The crowd cheers loudly in awe of Connors's resistance. As the second commentator Colin Long put it; the last shot was a bullet-like shot; hit with complete abandon for the winner.
Completely wrongfooted Connors again on those two aces; superb disguise.

Usually the players were just given a glass of water every changeover; but apparently Connors also requested tea and received a teapot and a cup on a teatray the ballboy put beside his chair - that's nice. // Both players made sure to towel the handle of their racquet dry before going back on court.

The umpire; as well as the commentators; calls it a 'tiebreaker' rather than a 'tiebreak'. While both words remain in use as of yet; I think official announcements only use ' tiebreak' now; so it's an interesting point to observe.

Right into the corner; but a mere centimetre wide. Connors playfully makes as if he were petrified by that miss; falling to the ground in despair; then gets up and gazes longingly towards the spot where the ball bounced. The fate of the match is decided by the smallest margins; as befits a great contest.
The elated crowd gives Newcombe a minute-long standing ovation - the umpire can't even finish stating the scoreline! Only gets to 'seven-five'.
